 the following:
 Order

This first bail application has been filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.608 of 2023 registered at Police Station Cantt. Distt. Guna (M.P.) for offences punishable under Section 363, 366-A, 376, 376(2)(n),
376(da) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in judicial custody since 14-08-2023.

As per the case of prosecution, father of victim reported to PS Cantt.
Guna that his daughter, aged around 13 years and 8 months, is missing since the night of 16-07-2023.
He suspects that some unknown person has allured and taken his minor daughter.

On such allegations, PS Cantt. Guna registered FIR at Crime No.608 of 2023 for offence punishable Ranjit Adiwasi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183635634/
1 under Section 363 of IPC against unknown offender.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Victim was recovered on 07.08.2023 from Fatehgarh Tiraha.
In her initial statement recorded U/s 161 of Cr.P.C on 07.08.2023, she stated that her parents wanted to marry her therefore, she left her parental home at her own.
She met Parvati Bai and stayed at the home of Parvati Bai at her own will.
Parwati was going to leave her to the parental home, police intercepted them and taken to the Police Station.
In her statement recorded same day, she stated on the same line.
Later, on 12.8.2023, in her supplementary statement recorded u/s 161 of Cr.P.C, she alleged that she wanted to marry accused Ranjeet, therefore, she left parental home.
Ranjeet took her to Bhador where she stayed with him as wife.
Ranjeet had physical relations with her which was known to his parents.
Ranjeet has allured and took her on the pretext of marriage and committed rape on her.
Again in her statement recorded u/s 164 of Cr.P.C before learned JMFC on 12.8.2023, victim resiled from her earlier statement and stated that Ranjeet has not committed any misdemeanor with her.
She stayed at village Bhador for some days and returned to her parents.
She had given the statement under pressure of her parents.
Applicant was arrested on 14.08.2023, he is in custody ever since.
After completion of investigation, final report was submitted on 20.8.2023.
In DNA report, no conclusive opinion was given as very low and uninterpretable Y-chromosome STR DNA profile was found.
Learned counsel for the applicant, in addition to the grounds mentioned in the application, submits that the applicant is falsely implicated in the matter.
The applicant is aged 18 years.
There was no physical relationship between the applicant and the victim.
Applicant is implicated under pressure of the family of victim.
No criminal antecedent is reported against the applicant.
There is no likelihood of his tampering with the evidence as both the parties belong to same socio-economic status.
There is no likelihood of his absconsion leaving behind his family and home.
No further custodial interrogation is required in the matter against the applicant as the investigation with regard to the applicant is almost complete.
Jail incarceration on false allegation is causing hardship to the young applicant.
Trial would take time to conclude.
Therefore, the applicant may be released on bail.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State opposed the bail application on the ground of gravity of alleged offence.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.

Considering the arguments advanced by both the parties and overall circumstances of the case, regard being had to the young age of the applicant, but without commenting on merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the applicant on bail.
Thus, the application is allowed.

Accordingly, it is directed that applicant RANJIT ADIWASI shall be released on bail in connection with Crime No.608 of 2023 registered at Police Station Cantt. Distt. Guna (M.P.) for offences punishable under Section 363, 366-A, 376, 376(2)(n), 376(da) of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act,
upon furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety of the same amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court, for compliance with the following conditions, :
Ranjit Adiwasi vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 18 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183635634/
